note.t: 2025 annual report, filed on paper (received May 14, 2026). This is a handwritten paper filing; values were read visually from the scanned checkboxes, so ranges are approximate. Assets of roughly $510K–$1.2M: a 41% stake in Venture Properties LLC, which owns three commercial rental properties in Anniston (1204 Quintard Ave. about $250K–$500K; 1310 Quintard Ave. $50K–$100K; 123 E. 13th St.), a 20% stake in Capital Development LLC ($50K–$100K; its sole asset is about 100 acres of land in Anniston; property-sale income $50,001–$100,000), his spouse's Noble Bank stock ($100K–$250K) and Southern Company stock ($15K–$50K), two Alfa whole-life policies, and his spouse's Retirement Systems of Alabama pension (value undetermined). Schedule B: sold his 50% interest in Initial Investments LLC (out of business) on Oct. 21, 2025 for $250,001–$500,000. Liabilities: a Shellpoint mortgage on the primary residence ($500K–$1M), a Congressional Federal Credit Union mortgage on a second (D.C.-area) residence noted as sold in March 2025 ($100K–$250K), and a Fifth Third auto loan ($10K–$15K). Spouse income sources: state judicial salary, Alabama retirement pension, Alabama Power retirement plan. Uncompensated positions in the three LLCs. No stock trades in defense companies; no foreign assets or income.

democracy.t: Recorded as 'Not Voting' on the objection to Ohio's 2004 electoral votes (House Roll Call 7; the objection failed 31–267).
Signed the House Republicans' December 2020 amicus brief backing Texas v. Pennsylvania, which sought to overturn results in four states; the Supreme Court declined the case.
Voted Yea on the objection to Arizona's electoral votes (failed 121–303).
Voted Yea on the objection to Pennsylvania's electoral votes (failed 138–282).
Was at the Capitol during the attack; the next day tweeted that 'there is no place for political violence in America.'
